html:
SMTO-GWT-0018 — The Gateway refused a request it had already received

GUID: b89ae679-f111-44a7-8a68-5fe10dbcf918
Slug: gateway-request-replayed
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • The Gateway received the exact same request a second time and refused the copy. The first copy may already have done its work.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the task and read its latest steps, or look on that computer, to see whether the action already happened. The first copy of the request may have finished even though this copy was refused.
  2. If it already happened, don't repeat it. Running it again would make the same change twice.
  3. If it didn't happen, run the task again. SMTO sends a brand-new request each time, which the Gateway will accept.
  4. If this message keeps coming back, ask whoever manages the network whether a proxy or other device resends traffic. Something on the network may be sending SMTO's requests twice.

What success looks like

  • You've confirmed the original action's result, and any new run finishes without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't repeat the action until you know whether the first request already carried it out.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Replay protection found the same controller and request nonce already pending or recorded, so the duplicate was rejected; the original request's effects are not settled by this rejection.

What this means

  • Replay protection found the same controller and nonce already pending, retained in memory or present in durable replay evidence. This rejects the duplicate, but does not settle the original request's effects. Rejecting the duplicate authenticates no new dispatch; earlier requests and their effects remain separate evidence.

Why this can happen

  • Replay protection found the same controller and nonce already pending, retained in memory or present in durable replay evidence. This rejects the duplicate, but does not settle the original request's effects.

How to diagnose it

  • Match the nonce rejection to the original operation and inspect its existing receipt or state before planning further work.

How to fix it

  • The (controller, nonce) pair was already pending, in memory or persisted within the 125-second replay window. Check the original operation's job status or receipt on the Gateway before sending any new change; new work must be freshly signed by the Server, and repeated duplicates suggest a retransmitting proxy or a client resending stored signed requests.
  • Inspect the original operation before sending another mutation. Let the existing authenticated protocol create fresh request identities only for justified new work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The original operation is reconciled; any separately authorized new action uses the protocol's fresh request identity.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Rejecting the duplicate authenticates no new dispatch; earlier requests and their effects remain separate evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
